title: Unit 1: The First 4 Consonants
subtitle: Hangul Baby Steps
description: Meet the simplest building blocks of Korean: ㄱ, ㄴ, ㄷ, ㄹ.

lessons.title: Meet ㄱ (Giyeok) & ㄴ (Nieun)
lessons.introduction: Korean letters look like pictures of sounds! Let's meet your very first two letters.

cards.mnemonic: Looks like an elbow or a corner. Makes a soft 'g' sound as in 'go'.
Looks like the side of a Nose! Makes the 'n' sound as in 'nest'.

storyPages.text: Baby Bear found a wooden corner stick shaped like 'ㄱ' in the forest.
A tiny butterfly landed right on his Nose, which looked like 'ㄴ'!
Now Baby Bear remembers: Corner is 'ㄱ' (g) and Nose is 'ㄴ' (n)!

lessons.title: Meet ㄷ (Digeut) & ㄹ (Rieul)
lessons.introduction: You mastered ㄱ and ㄴ! Now let's meet two friendly steps forward: ㄷ and ㄹ.

cards.mnemonic: Looks like an open Doorway! Makes the 'd' sound as in 'door'.
Curvy like a winding Road or snake! Makes an 'r' / 'l' sound.

story.title: The Door and the Winding Road

storyPages.text: Baby Bear opened the Door 'ㄷ' to start his morning adventure.
He walked down the winding Road 'ㄹ' toward the sparkling river.

questions.prompt: Which letter looks like a Nose and sounds like 'n'?
questions.explanation: ㄴ represents the tongue touching the roof of mouth, shaped like a Nose ('n').

questions.prompt: Listen to the sound and choose the matching Korean consonant:
questions.explanation: You heard 'g' which is ㄱ (Giyeok)!

questions.prompt: Which letter looks like an open Door ('d')?
questions.explanation: ㄷ is shaped like a Door and produces the 'd' sound.

questions.prompt: What sound does ㄹ (winding road) make?
questions.explanation: ㄹ sounds like a light flap 'r' or 'l'.

questions.prompt: Trace the letter ㄱ with your finger on the screen!
options: Trace ㄱ with your finger to complete!
questions.explanation: Super job! ㄱ is a top horizontal stroke followed by a vertical drop.

questions.prompt: Listen carefully. Which consonant matches this sound?
questions.explanation: You heard the 'd' sound, which is ㄷ (Digeut - Door)!

questions.prompt: Listen to the audio. Which letter corresponds to this sound?
questions.explanation: You heard the 'n' sound, which corresponds to ㄴ (Nieun - Nose)!

questions.prompt: Which consonant is shaped like a corner or gun, representing the back of the tongue?
questions.explanation: ㄱ (Giyeok) represents the tongue blocking the throat at a 90-degree corner!

questions.prompt: In the word '고양이' (Goyang-i - Cat), what is the starting consonant sound?
questions.explanation: 고양이 begins with 'ㄱ', making the soft 'g' sound!

questions.prompt: Which letter represents a winding road or rattlesnake?
questions.explanation: ㄹ (Rieul) has a zig-zag snake or winding road shape!

questions.prompt: Match the word '나비' (Nabi - Butterfly) with its starting letter:
questions.explanation: 나비 (Butterfly) starts with 'ㄴ' (n)!

questions.prompt: Trace the letter ㄴ (Nieun) with your finger on the screen!
questions.explanation: Awesome! ㄴ starts from the top vertical stroke and turns right horizontally.

questions.prompt: Trace the letter ㄷ (Digeut) with your finger on the screen!
questions.explanation: Great work! ㄷ is drawn with a top horizontal stroke, then an L-shaped base.

questions.prompt: Which consonant starts the Korean word '다람쥐' (Daramjwi - Squirrel)?
questions.explanation: 다람쥐 begins with ㄷ (d)!

title: Unit 2: Basic Vowels (ㅏ, ㅓ, ㅗ, ㅜ)
subtitle: Breathing Life with Vowels
description: Consonants need vowels to speak! Learn the primary 4 vowel sounds.

lessons.title: Bright Vowels: ㅏ (a) & ㅗ (o)
lessons.introduction: Vowels are made of the Sky (•), Earth (ㅡ), and Person (ㅣ).

cards.mnemonic: A person pointing right towards the bright sun: 'Ah!'.
The sun rising above the horizon line: 'Oh! sunrise!'.

storyPages.text: The sun pops up above the earth: 'ㅗ' (o)!

questions.prompt: Which vowel sounds like 'ah' in 'father'?
questions.explanation: ㅏ produces the open 'ah' sound!

questions.prompt: Which vowel represents the sun rising ABOVE the horizon line?
questions.explanation: ㅗ represents the bright sun pointing upward above the earth horizon ('o')!

questions.prompt: Listen to the vowel sound and choose the correct letter:
questions.explanation: You heard 'o' as in 'open' or 'boat', which is ㅗ!

questions.prompt: Which vowel has a horizontal ground with a vertical line pointing DOWN under the earth?
questions.explanation: ㅜ points downward beneath the horizon, making the 'oo' sound as in 'moon'!

questions.prompt: Listen carefully. Which vowel matches this sound?
questions.explanation: You heard the open 'ah' sound, which is ㅏ!

questions.prompt: What sound does the vowel ㅓ make?
questions.explanation: ㅓ has an inward stroke pointing left, sounding like 'eo' or 'uh' as in 'sun'!

questions.prompt: In Korean vowel philosophy, what does the vertical standing line (ㅣ) represent?
questions.explanation: In Hangul, • is Sky/Sun, ㅡ is Earth/Ground, and ㅣ is the upright standing Person!

questions.prompt: Which vowel starts the Korean word '오이' (Oi - Cucumber)?
questions.explanation: 오이 starts with ㅗ ('o')!

questions.prompt: Trace the vowel ㅏ (Ah) with your finger on the screen!
questions.explanation: Splendid! Vertical line first from top to bottom, then the middle short stroke to the right.

questions.prompt: Trace the vowel ㅗ (Oh) with your finger on the screen!
questions.explanation: Well done! Short top vertical stroke first, then the long horizontal base line.

title: Unit 3: Syllable Blocks (가, 나, 다, 라)
subtitle: Combining Consonant + Vowel
description: In Korean, letters snap together into cute syllable boxes like LEGO blocks!

lessons.title: Building Blocks: ㄱ + ㅏ = 가
lessons.introduction: Watch magic happen: snap consonant 'ㄱ' and vowel 'ㅏ' side-by-side to make '가' (Ga)!

storyPages.text: Baby Bear packed his bag to go: '가' (Ga)!
He pointed happily at himself: '나' (Na - Me)!

questions.prompt: What syllable do you get when you combine 'ㄱ' (g) and 'ㅏ' (a)?
questions.explanation: ㄱ + ㅏ = 가 (Ga)!

questions.prompt: What does the syllable '나' (ㄴ + ㅏ) mean in Korean?
questions.explanation: 나 (Na) is the Korean word for 'I' or 'Me'!

questions.prompt: Which syllable block combines the consonant 'ㄷ' (d) and vowel 'ㅏ' (a)?
questions.explanation: ㄷ + ㅏ snaps together to form '다' (Da)!

questions.prompt: Listen to the syllable sound and choose the matching block:
questions.explanation: You heard '가' (Ga)!

questions.prompt: Listen to the audio. Which syllable block is being spoken?
questions.explanation: You heard '나' (Na)!

questions.prompt: Combine 'ㄹ' (r/l) and 'ㅏ' (a). Which syllable is formed?
questions.explanation: ㄹ + ㅏ combines into '라' (Ra/La)!

questions.prompt: The word '가방' (bag) begins with which syllable block?
questions.explanation: 가방 (bag) starts with 가 (ga)!

questions.prompt: The word '나무' (tree) begins with which syllable block?
questions.explanation: 나무 (tree) starts with 나 (na)!

questions.prompt: Trace the syllable block 가 (Ga) with your finger!
questions.explanation: Brilliant! You wrote consonant ㄱ on the left, and vowel ㅏ on the right!

questions.prompt: Trace the syllable block 나 (Na) with your finger!
questions.explanation: Outstanding! ㄴ sits on the left and ㅏ stands on the right to form 나!
